source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Identify the specific areas or systems that did not comply with fire-safety standards. Clearly mark each failed item on the inspection report, attaching photographs or diagrams when possible. Include exact locations within the building.

3. Conduct a thorough investigation to determine the reasons behind the failure. This may involve inspecting equipment, interviewing maintenance personnel, or consulting technical manuals. Document all findings in detail.

4. Use standardized checklists or templates to document the failed items, ensuring all relevant information is captured accurately. This includes the date and time of inspection, the identity of the inspector, the nature of the failure, and the implications on fire safety.

5. Cite specific regulations or standards that were not met. This will involve referring to local building codes, fire codes, and other legal requirements.

6. Propose corrective measures for each failed item. These should be detailed, feasible, and include an estimated timeframe for completion. Indicate whether professional technicians or specific skill
